workflow.title: Plan an at-risk release
workflow.question: This release is at risk. What can we still commit to?
workflow.description: Compare four complete release arrangements against remaining validation work, scoped qualifications, working intervals, resource commitments, additional spending, recorded prerequisites and permission. Keep the original scope and deadline distinct from explicitly accepted revisions. This bounded calculation does not predict delivery probabilities or replace a ticket system.

definition.title: Complete a commitment
definition.description: Determine whether one complete static plan can satisfy every mandatory obligation across every explicitly admitted scenario. Compare feasible plans only after whole-plan execution feasibility is established.

authoring.guidance:
What must be completed, for whom, and within which accepted limits?
Which objects, quantities, revisions and locations are covered?
Which factual records and admitted states are we relying on?
Which complete choices may the planner make?
Which activities, dependencies, calendars and capacities must the same plan respect?
Which scoped permissions must cover each required operation?
Which joint operating scenarios must this commitment withstand?
Which obligations are mandatory, and how will passing complete plans be compared?
Module authors supply these declarations and domain vocabulary. Case workers supply only values allowed by the frozen module. Facts, scenarios and operating permission must never be inferred from a preferred plan.

definition.title: Complete a commitment
definition.responsibility: Find one complete static operating choice that satisfies every mandatory obligation across every explicitly admitted joint scenario, then compare feasible choices.
invariants: Choices are finite, input-only controls. One complete assignment is shared across every admitted scenario and obligation.
Admitted joint scenarios are explicit facts; neither independence, probabilities nor unlisted scenarios are inferred.
An empty admitted basis is inconsistent, never a vacuous feasibility result.
Typed acyclic expressions separate static controls, scenario consequences and post-scenario preference aggregates.
Activities, calendars, bookings and permission validity use half-open intervals; adjacent intervals do not overlap.
Capacity is the sum of simultaneous renewable demands. A scoped grant must cover its entire required operation.
Expense sums nonrefundable charges. Refundable holds affect cash only; simultaneous cash events are netted before peak cash is measured.
Every mandatory condition must pass for the same choice in every admitted scenario. Preference cannot compensate for failure.
Ranking is lexicographic over feasible choices only; genuine ties are retained and identifiers only stabilize display order.
A fully checked witness establishes existence during partial search. No-plan and optimality claims require complete relevant coverage.
Missing data, unresolved lookups, unsafe arithmetic and unsupported declarations are invalid input, never invented facts.
Calculated feasibility is conditional on accepted facts and fixed assumptions, not permission, reservation or evidence of actual completion.

expressionLanguage.literals: Finite scalar or homogeneous scalar-array data; no executable code.

operators.add: At least two compatible numbers -> number
operators.mul: Two numbers with at most one dimensional operand -> number; count is a multiplicity
operators.lookup: Complete primary-key binding in a typed input table -> exactly one selected scalar; missing or ambiguous lookup is invalid
operators.exists: Typed equality bindings plus optional row-scoped predicate -> boolean; no match is false
operators.interval-covered: Typed selected calendar rows and a positive half-open interval -> boolean; adjacent coverage may combine
operators.worst-case: Numeric expression -> maximum across admitted scenarios for preference only; nested or unreduced scenario aggregates are invalid

caseDerivation: All case parameters and keyed input rows use the frozen module.inputs types, units, bounds, keys and references; no missing-value defaults or coercion are inferred.
Finite choices draw only from input arrays, input table columns or fixed literal domains; the same assignment applies to every scenario.
The scenarioDomain table explicitly lists admitted joint scenarios; an empty table is an inconsistent basis rather than vacuous feasibility.
Activity graphs, constraints, mandatory obligations, resource mappings, financial mode and preference remain frozen module declarations.
Provenance describes accepted factual sources; identifying a source does not authenticate it or infer readiness.
schema.description: Installed closed typed declaration and case-admission validators; this descriptor is not a complete JSON Schema. Publication checks admission, not computed feasibility.

structuralSlots.description: Declare one time origin, common time and money units, and additional numeric units.
Declare required typed parameters and keyed relations.
Declare finite static controls from input-only domains.
Bind the input relation containing explicit joint scenarios.
Bind typed acyclic consequences using the installed expression language.
Declare static activity actors, timing and renewable resource demands.
Map resource capacities and existing bookings.
Name and explain every mandatory commitment obligation.
Bind predicates and shared resource-capacity checks to obligations.
Declare nonrefundable charges and optional timed refundable holds.
Optionally require complete finite lookup coverage.
Supply domain vocabulary without changing calculations.
State accepted premises and the applicability boundary.

caseInputs.description: Supply every declared parameter, including finite choice grids and current limits.
Supply typed records, accepted scenarios, calendars, grants, resources and other declared facts.
Record the accepted source and scope of supplied information.

responsibilities: Complete candidate assignments and all checked scenarios
Activities, interval/resource checks and scoped permission traces
Expense, timed cash events and peak cash where declared

definitionContract.title: Complete a commitment
definitionContract.responsibility: Find one complete static operating choice that satisfies every mandatory obligation across every explicitly admitted joint scenario, then compare feasible choices.
invariants: Choices are finite, input-only controls. One complete assignment is shared across every admitted scenario and obligation.
Admitted joint scenarios are explicit facts; neither independence, probabilities nor unlisted scenarios are inferred.
An empty admitted basis is inconsistent, never a vacuous feasibility result.
Typed acyclic expressions separate static controls, scenario consequences and post-scenario preference aggregates.
Activities, calendars, bookings and permission validity use half-open intervals; adjacent intervals do not overlap.
Capacity is the sum of simultaneous renewable demands. A scoped grant must cover its entire required operation.
Expense sums nonrefundable charges. Refundable holds affect cash only; simultaneous cash events are netted before peak cash is measured.
Every mandatory condition must pass for the same choice in every admitted scenario. Preference cannot compensate for failure.
Ranking is lexicographic over feasible choices only; genuine ties are retained and identifiers only stabilize display order.
A fully checked witness establishes existence during partial search. No-plan and optimality claims require complete relevant coverage.
Missing data, unresolved lookups, unsafe arithmetic and unsupported declarations are invalid input, never invented facts.
Calculated feasibility is conditional on accepted facts and fixed assumptions, not permission, reservation or evidence of actual completion.

expressionLanguage.literals: Finite scalar or homogeneous scalar-array data; no executable code.

operators.add: At least two compatible numbers -> number
operators.mul: Two numbers with at most one dimensional operand -> number; count is a multiplicity
operators.lookup: Complete primary-key binding in a typed input table -> exactly one selected scalar; missing or ambiguous lookup is invalid
operators.exists: Typed equality bindings plus optional row-scoped predicate -> boolean; no match is false
operators.interval-covered: Typed selected calendar rows and a positive half-open interval -> boolean; adjacent coverage may combine
operators.worst-case: Numeric expression -> maximum across admitted scenarios for preference only; nested or unreduced scenario aggregates are invalid

module.title: Compare release arrangements
module.question: Which supplied release arrangements can satisfy the recorded scope, deadline, QA and spending requirements?
module.description: Compare four complete arrangements for an at-risk release. Reduced scope and a later date remain explicit amendments to the original commitment. This bounded calculation does not certify release quality or search all possible schedules.

units.timeOrigin: minutes from the recorded release-planning origin

assumptions: Inputs describe fictional remaining QA work and recorded qualifications. Unknown workload or missing required facts leave the comparison unavailable; ticket status is not acceptance evidence.

Core QA includes 240 minutes of independent regression and 60 minutes of integration sign-off. Primary core QA is the remaining recorded core work. Reporting QA is added to integration when included. All intervals are half-open working minutes.

The existing QA resource represents one exclusive qualified allocation. Concurrent outside bookings reduce its availability through the shared capacity check. The additional QA resource can perform the authored independent regression package only.

These four supplied schedules are not an exhaustive release scheduler. A different task dependency, a different transferable work package or a changed staffing structure requires an authored model revision.
The original full scope and original deadline are retained in every outcome. A passing amended arrangement does not meet the original commitment unchanged.
The additional fee is a flat accepted amount for the complete engagement, in currency cents; existing sunk costs and unmodeled quality risks are not estimated.
Recorded prerequisite confirmation and authority do not authenticate an approver, perform tests, change the product scope, publish a release or prove successful operation.

requirements.label: Recorded release scope
requirements.meaning: Core QA is retained. Deferring reporting requires an explicitly accepted scope amendment for this release.

requirements.label: Recorded release deadline
requirements.meaning: All QA and the complete handoff finish by the original deadline or a proposed deadline matching the explicitly accepted revised deadline.

requirements.label: Qualified QA for this build
requirements.meaning: Each actual QA resource has a qualification covering this build, environment and full assigned interval.

requirements.label: Whole-activity availability
requirements.meaning: Recorded working availability covers every complete assigned activity.

requirements.label: Exclusive QA and handoff resources
requirements.meaning: Activities and existing bookings cannot use the same exclusive resource simultaneously.

requirements.label: Confirmed release prerequisite
requirements.meaning: The recorded prerequisite is confirmed; a ticket status alone does not establish it.

requirements.label: Recorded release authority
requirements.meaning: The recorded release authorization is present. This does not obtain an external approval.

requirements.label: Additional spending limit
requirements.meaning: The flat accepted fee for the complete additional QA engagement fits the recorded limit.

requirements.label: Authored arrangement meaning
requirements.meaning: Case inputs cannot rewrite which scope, deadline or resources an arrangement represents.

provenance.description: Fictional remaining work, recorded working windows, qualifications and accepted amendment facts. This calculation neither certifies software quality nor records an external approval or deployment.

questions.label: Remaining core validation
questions.question: How much core validation work remains?
questions.meaning: Remaining core QA effort, in whole minutes, across the authored base, independent and integration phases. This bounded profile requires at least 301 minutes; changing the activity structure requires an adapted app.

questions.label: Remaining reporting validation
questions.question: How much reporting validation work remains?
questions.meaning: Remaining reporting QA effort in whole minutes. Reporting is included in the original release; deferring it is an explicit scope revision.

questions.label: Original release deadline
questions.question: When was the complete original release promised?
questions.meaning: The original commitment deadline, in whole minutes from the declared calendar origin. A later proposal does not replace this baseline.

questions.label: Proposed later deadline
questions.question: What later deadline could be accepted?
questions.meaning: A proposed revised release deadline on the same clock. Supplying a date does not establish acceptance of that change.

questions.label: Deadline named in the amendment record
questions.question: Which exact revised deadline does the recorded acceptance cover?
questions.meaning: The precise deadline named in the amendment record, in whole minutes from the same origin. It is operative only when the later-deadline acceptance flag is true and it matches the proposed deadline. A changed proposal does not inherit an earlier acceptance.

questions.label: Additional expense limit
questions.question: How much additional expense is available for a complete arrangement?
questions.meaning: The complete additional-expense limit in USD cents. This is a spending boundary, not a valuation of deferred reporting or delayed delivery.

questions.label: Complete additional-help fee
questions.question: What is the complete fee for the additional qualified help?
questions.meaning: The flat additional expense in USD cents for the authored additional-help arrangement. A low fee does not establish qualification, availability or release permission.

questions.label: Scope revision accepted
questions.question: Has deferring reporting been accepted for this release?
questions.meaning: Recorded acceptance of the specific core-only revision. A passing revised arrangement still does not satisfy the original complete-scope promise.

questions.label: Later deadline accepted
questions.question: Has the proposed later release deadline been accepted?
questions.meaning: Recorded acceptance of the specific later-deadline revision. The original deadline remains visible.

questions.label: Release prerequisites established
questions.question: Are the declared release prerequisites established?
questions.meaning: The scoped prerequisite finding supplied for this build and validation environment. Ticket status is not evidence of this finding. This pilot does not independently assess the underlying records.

questions.label: Recorded release permission
questions.question: Is permission recorded for this release?
questions.meaning: Recorded operating permission for the authored release. The calculation does not authenticate a person or obtain permission.

questions.label: Validation working intervals
questions.question: When can the listed resources perform validation and handoff?
questions.meaning: Complete working intervals on the shared minute clock. Gaps represent unavailable time; effort and elapsed time are different quantities.

questions.label: Scoped validation qualifications
questions.question: Which resources are qualified for this build and environment?
questions.meaning: Qualification intervals must cover the actual work for the authored build and environment. An extra person alone does not establish usable validation capacity.

questions.label: Other resource commitments
questions.question: Which other commitments consume the same resources?
questions.meaning: Retained bookings on the same resource identities and clock. An empty list means none are recorded; missing information must remain unanswered.

value.scope: A finite comparison of four complete release arrangements using one declared activity structure, scoped qualifications and recorded operating facts.
assumptions: Remaining effort is a reviewed whole-minute estimate; it is not inferred from ticket status or story points.
The authored QA phases distinguish sequential dependencies from work that can be performed by qualified additional help. Effort totals alone do not establish finish times.
Working intervals, qualifications and other commitments refer to the same build, validation environment and clock.
Cost is additional complete expense, not a modeled value of deferred reporting or delayed delivery. No financial or delivery preference is declared.
An unknown required input leaves the whole comparison unresolved. This bounded pilot does not claim partial per-arrangement conclusions or predict delivery probabilities.
